beats.say: Every team at Cymbal wants a database.
The catalog, the carts, price history, sessions, and product images.
beats.label: They all want one

beats.say: There is no one best store. Pick by how the data is read and written.
beats.label: Station 3.1 · Selecting storage
beats.head: Pick by how it is read and written

check.prompt: Billions of sensor readings, very fast writes, and lookups by key. Which store?
check.why: Bigtable is built for huge key-value data with fast writes.

beats.say: Ask four questions, in this order.
Analytics or transactions? Relational or not? How big, and how global? And how fast?
beats.label: In order

beats.say: Analytics over huge data, with SQL? That is BigQuery.
beats.label: Analytics
beats.head: BigQuery
beats.text: A warehouse. Not an app database.

beats.say: Files, images and backups go to Cloud Storage.
beats.label: Files and blobs
beats.head: Cloud Storage

beats.say: A normal relational app, in one region? Cloud SQL.
beats.label: Relational, one region
beats.head: Cloud SQL

beats.say: Relational, but global, with strong consistency? Spanner.
beats.label: Relational, global
beats.head: Spanner

beats.say: Huge key-value data, with very fast writes, like sensors? Bigtable.
beats.label: Huge and fast
beats.head: Bigtable

beats.say: Documents for a mobile app? Firestore. A cache? Memorystore.
beats.label: Two more
beats.head: Documents: Firestore. Cache: Memorystore.

beats.say: The trap: BigQuery as an app database, for single row lookups and updates.
beats.label: Exam trap

check.prompt: Which row key avoids a hotspot?
check.why: A key that starts with the sensor ID spreads the writes across servers.

beats.say: Bigtable has one index only: the row key.
Rows are stored sorted by key, like words in a dictionary.
beats.label: How it is stored
beats.head: Sorted, like a dictionary

beats.say: So if every key starts with the time, all new writes land on one server. A hotspot.
beats.label: The danger
beats.head: Key starts with a timestamp = hotspot

beats.say: The fix: start the key with something that spreads, like the sensor ID. Then the time.
beats.label: The fix
beats.head: sensorId#timestamp

beats.say: And design the key around your most common query.
beats.label: The rule
beats.head: Design the key for your main query

beats.say: Next, the relational family, in one line each.
Cloud SQL scales up, not out. High availability adds a standby in another zone.
beats.label: Cloud SQL
beats.head: Scales up. HA standby in another zone.

beats.say: AlloyDB is PostgreSQL that is also fast for analytics.
beats.label: AlloyDB
beats.head: PostgreSQL, fast at analytics too

beats.say: Spanner scales out across the world, with 99.999 percent availability.
Memorystore is a cache. Never make it your system of record.
beats.label: Exam trap
beats.text: Memorystore is a cache, not the system of record.

check.prompt: How is the Archive class different from Standard?
options: It costs less to store and more to read
check.why: All classes have the same speed and durability. Only the prices differ.

beats.say: Now Cloud Storage. Four classes, by how often you read.
Standard for hot data. Nearline for monthly. Coldline for quarterly. Archive for yearly.
beats.label: By how often you read

beats.say: Here is the surprise. All four are equally fast and equally safe.
beats.label: The surprise
beats.head: Same speed. Same durability.

beats.say: Colder classes are cheaper to store, but you pay to read, and for deleting early.
beats.label: The trade
beats.head: Cheaper to store, costly to read

beats.say: Lifecycle rules move objects for you. Autoclass does it when you do not know the pattern.
beats.label: Automation
beats.head: Lifecycle rules. Or Autoclass.

beats.say: For compliance, a retention policy with Bucket Lock makes objects impossible to delete.
beats.label: Compliance
beats.head: Retention policy + Bucket Lock

beats.say: Last: let time save you money.
In BigQuery, a table you have not changed for 90 days gets cheaper by itself.
beats.sub: untouched days, then about half price

beats.say: So do not export old tables to Cloud Storage just to save money.
beats.label: Exam trap
beats.text: Exporting old BigQuery data just to save money

beats.say: And set an expiration on data you do not need. It deletes itself.
beats.label: Housekeeping
beats.head: Set an expiration

beats.say: Recap.
Four questions pick the store. The row key is Bigtable's only index.
beats.label: Station 3.1 · 1 of 2

beats.say: Storage classes share speed, not price. And old BigQuery data gets cheaper by itself.
beats.label: Station 3.1 · 2 of 2
